When we speak of how our perception of people changes over time, Robert Pattinson is quite an example.. For many millennials and zillennials, he'll probably always have a little Edward Cullen attached to him. I know I do. The mysterious vampire from the Twilight saga who became a cultural phenomenon. And before that, he was Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. Quite a journey.. if you think about it!

What's more interesting is what he did after becoming so closely associated with one character. He didn't spend his career recreating a similar character. Instead, he explored very different roles, with Tenet, and eventually gave us a rather impressive, brooding Bruce Wayne / Batman... And parallelly to this.. our perception of him changed too.. 
For some, he's a teenage obsession. For others, he's Batman. And for those who've followed his career more closely, he's an actor comfortable moving between mainstream cinema and unconventional filmmaking.

Pattinson has always had an interesting public persona too. His dry humour, eccentric interviews and rather unconventional approach makes him stand out. At the same time, he represents luxury houses like Dior and Jaeger-LeCoultre, bringing his own individuality to worlds rooted in heritage and craftsmanship.

From Edward Cullen to Bruce Wayne, and now James Bond, audiences have seen him take on very different identities... And perhaps that's what makes his journey interesting: the ability to evolve, explore different facets and still remain recognizable. I feel that's the interesting part of personal branding: evolving without losing what makes you recognizable.
comment: The real test of personal branding is whether an audience can accept your next move without feeling you've abandoned your identity. That transition takes consistency, not just reinvention.
